articleBody:
Before your contractor closes up shower walls with tile or marble, you have one crucial window to verify the moisture barrier. Catching a missed detail now prevents costly tear-outs later. Use this checklist during your rough-in inspection.

- [ ] Confirm substrate is clean and free of loose debris — Trapped dust and sharp protrusions can puncture membranes or prevent proper bonding.
- [ ] Check shower pan slope to drain — Substrates must pitch steadily toward the drain so water flows away freely without standing.
- [ ] Inspect corner and joint reinforcement — Every change of plane, floor seam, and wall junction must have embedded reinforcement tape or preformed corners.
- [ ] Verify pipe penetrations have elastomeric seals — Shower valve cutouts and supply pipes need tight-fitting waterproof collars, not just open caulk.
- [ ] Measure wall membrane coverage height — Waterproofing should extend high enough to protect wall studs from spray, especially in enclosed showers.
- [ ] Check membrane thickness for consistency — Liquid-applied membranes require uniform application without pinholes, voids, or thin patches.
- [ ] Verify proper manufacturer cure times — Membranes must dry fully before anyone walks on the pan or applies heavy mortar.
- [ ] Conduct a water leak test on the pan — Plugging the drain and filling the basin checks the assembly before finish tiles cover the floor.

How to use this checklist:
Walk the bathroom with your lead contractor before tiling starts to confirm each item is completed and documented.
